design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (member_cost_sharing_and_renewal, category plan)

1. Why this is a good test. The mother of a CHIP Kids child (Zuri Halvorsen-Mbeki, open membership, coverage from 2025-11-01) asks only for a refund of copays paid above the family's yearly limit. The scored refund (265.98) sits behind three prerequisite problems the charter states and the records show unmet: a past-due premium month the family must pay itself (user tool), specialist-rated visits of the child's own primary care providers owed a re-rating, and office visits the primary care visit log shows as preventive or coordinated care owed a preventive re-rating. Each of the four writes is a multi-factor computation over reconciled ledgers (claims, premiums) and cross-difficulty records (pcp assignments and visit log, rx fills, auth authorizations, ride trips) plus care-management records. Difficulty comes from reading the charter, discovering the unmet states and computing four numbers in dependency order, never from picking among tools (each tool has one business meaning).

2. Scope. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[6,6,6,4]; realised: over-cap refund 6, past-due premium payment 6, office-visit preventive re-rating 6, own-PCP visit re-rating 4. Claimed: plan_ext_over_cap_refund (root, tool book_over_cap_refund_b068d625), plan_ext_past_due_premium_payment (user, pay_past_due_premium_fdc43b6b), plan_ext_own_pcp_visit_rerating (book_own_pcp_visit_rerating_ea94b99c), plan_ext_office_visit_preventive_rerating (book_office_visit_rerating_0e97c2c0). Occupied before: nothing. Left for task 1 (draw 2 prerequisite problems, factor counts [5,5,6]): a membership ended for premium non-payment (lockout balance payment by the family, user tool) with two claims-side re-ratings of other classes (a rehabilitation therapy course under an approved authorization; ambulance transports of a wheelchair-van-dependent child), none of which this task's tools or policies touch; in this task's world both of those re-ratings evaluate to 0.00 (no therapy authorization, no ambulance claim).

3. Problem-tree card (fan-out, all edges state form, all value_input).
 - over-cap refund <- past-due premium payment. Sentence (affirmative, own rule): "On a membership that is still open, the over-cap refund is fixed only after the premium balance on the membership stands at zero." State: premium_balance of the open membership = 0.00. Seed: plan_memberships.<m0>.premium_balance = 35.0 (the 2026-08 bill of 35.00 has no payment). Only one write of the difficulty brings a zero balance on an OPEN membership: the family's past-due payment (the task-1 lockout payment acts on memberships ended for non-payment). Kind value_input (gate premium_counted): the counted premium moves from 'premiums paid less the balance' to 'premiums paid'. Skipping it: refund 219.22 instead of 267.97 and no payment row.
 - over-cap refund <- own-PCP visit re-rating. Sentence (affirmative): "The over-cap refund is fixed only after the visits the member's own primary care provider billed under the specialist visit copay in the counting window carry their re-rating adjustment entry." Seed: claim C26-0714-45006 (NPI 1467283015 = current PCP) member_cost_share 10.0 specialist_visit, no adjustment row. Only the own-PCP re-rating books such an entry. Skipping: refund 303.97.
 - over-cap refund <- office-visit preventive re-rating. Sentence (negated direction, chosen because a claims desk states a reconciliation 'is not worked out until' corrections stand): "The over-cap refund is not worked out until the office visits the member's primary care providers billed under the primary care visit copay in the counting window carry their preventive re-rating adjustment entry." Seed: C26-0706-45077 copay 5.0, visit log follow_up, no adjustment row. Skipping: refund 304.97.
 - Four-point test per sentence: ordering connective (only after / not until); XX is a record-visible state (a balance, an adjustment entry standing); no tool, id or snake_case token; scope exactly the batch the depended-on rule defines. Derivation: sentence + claims/premium ledger + the depended-on rule ('booked as one adjustment entry that names the most recently serviced claim of the batch', 'settles that month') -> exactly one write each.
 - Topological order used by gold: own-PCP re-rating (step 15), office-visit re-rating (17), payment (19, user), refund (21). Parallel prerequisites commute: sim.py replay in reverse order P2-W-K1-P1 gives 13.75 / 37.00 / 36.00 / 267.97 and a byte-identical terminal DB.
 - user_scenario names no prerequisite (no premium, bill, visit type or re-rating); the tools validate nothing (single ctx.create; the payment also updates the balance).

4. Factor cards (handling-time world; baseline figure = result with that factor at its fall-through).
 over-cap refund = 267.97 (all-baseline 0.00: cap 1607.40 at 5% x 12 months exceeds the counted total).
  - cap_percent_by_income_and_authorized_care (parameter, multi-source income AND auth, cross-difficulty auth): income 152% <= 185 and DME authorization PA-2602-118457 approved on a request received 2026-02-09 -> 2.5%; baseline 5% -> 0.00. Near-miss: the occupational-therapy authorization PA-2507-109233 was received 2025-07-02, outside the 12-month window, and is expired.
  - cap_months_by_coverage_span (method): coverage started 2025-11-01, 9 whole months before the review month -> 9 months (2025-11..2026-07); baseline 12 -> 67.05.
  - counted_premium_by_premium_standing (method): after the payment the balance is 0.00 -> premiums paid in window 193.75 (nine months at 20.00 incl. 2026-07, plus 13.75 today); baseline 0 -> 74.22.
  - admission_relief_credit (parameter, multi-source): 3 paid inpatient stays (2026-01-06, 04-02, 06-30) AND active Care Coordination Level 2 -> 150.00; baseline 0 -> 117.97. Near-miss: the 2025-10-14 stay is on the ended Children's Medicaid spell.
  - medication_relief_credit (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty rx): 6 paid refills in the window and no rejection -> 60.00; baseline 0 -> 207.97. Near-miss: the Tdap vaccine fill is a new fill, not a refill.
  - travel_relief_credit (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty ride): 7 completed trips AND RideLink Mileage Reimbursement -> 50.00; baseline 0 -> 217.97.
  Counted total 610.75 = medical copays net 417.00 (490.00 booked less 36.00 and 37.00 re-rating entries) + refunds 0 + pharmacy 0.00 (PrairieRx Children) + premium 193.75. Cap = 2679.00 x 9 x 2.5 / 100 = 602.775, rounded half up to 602.78 (the rule states half up and the compute adds a sub-cent guard before rounding, so the tie resolves the same way on both faces), less 150.00 + 60.00 + 50.00 of relief = 342.78. Refund 610.75 - 342.78 = 267.97.
 past-due premium payment = 13.75 (all-baseline 35.00).
  - month_rate_under_continuous_eligibility (method): CE running 8 of 12 months AND bill 35.00 > last paid 20.00 -> 20.00; baseline 35.00 -> 28.75.
  - well_child_reward (parameter, cross-difficulty pcp): 3 well-child visits logged in 12 months (2026-02-17 in person, 2026-03-24 telehealth, 2026-04-21 in person), at least the minimum of 2, AND PCMH practice -> 3.00; baseline 0 -> 15.25.
  - refill_reward (parameter, cross-difficulty rx): 4 paid fills in 6 months (03-05, 04-18, 06-02 and the 06-16 vaccine), at least the minimum of 3, and no rejection -> 2.00; baseline 0 -> 15.75. Near-miss: the 2026-01-27 refill is 6 whole months back and falls outside.
  - care_reward (parameter): active episode AND 2 reached contacts in 3 months -> 2.50; baseline 0 -> 15.00.
  - steady_payer_reward (parameter): 7 portal + 2 phone payments -> 1.50; baseline 0 -> 15.25.
  - reward_stacking (method): PCMH AND active episode -> (3.00 + 2.50)/2 + 2.00 + 1.50 = 6.25; baseline all added 9.00 -> 11.00.
 own-PCP visit re-rating = 36.00 (all-baseline 15.00).
  - batch_scope_by_assignment_history (method, pcp): previous Riverfront assignment superseded AND Heartland assignment member-selected -> current provider from 2026-03 (C26-0310-42741, C26-0714-45006) plus previous provider (C26-1216-41002, C26-0120-41793): 4 visits, 40.00; baseline current provider over the whole window (3 visits incl. C26-0112-41640 of 2026-01-12, before Dr. Koury was PCP) -> 28.00. Near-miss: C26-0112-41640.
  - rerated_copay_by_practice_type (parameter, pcp): Patient-Centered Medical Home Practice -> 2.00; baseline 5.00 -> 30.00.
  - telehealth_followup_copay (parameter, pcp): telehealth follow-up 2026-07-14 AND medical home -> 0.00; baseline 2.00 -> 34.00.
  - initial_appointment_copay (parameter, pcp): initial health appointment 2026-03-10, 9 days after the 2026-03-01 effective date -> 0.00; baseline 2.00 -> 34.00.
 office-visit preventive re-rating = 37.00 (all-baseline 10.00: the two logged well-child visits returned in full, every other visit keeps its copay).
  - Preventive part (not a factor, base plan_evt_copay): well-child visits 2026-02-17 (superseded log) and 2026-04-21 (current log) return 5.00 each; no tier ever leaves a copay on preventive care.
  - telehealth_sick_log_scope (method, pcp): superseded previous assignment -> telehealth sick visits of both logs (2026-02-10 superseded, 2026-03-24 current); baseline current log only -> 33.00.
  - telehealth_sick_visit_copay (parameter, pcp): medical home -> 1.00; baseline 5.00 -> 29.00.
  - same_day_sick_visit_copay (parameter, pcp): sick visit C26-0421-43391 on 2026-04-21, the latest well-child day, medical home -> 0.00; baseline -> 32.00.
  - vaccine_day_sick_visit_copay (parameter, cross-difficulty rx): sick visit C26-0616-44420 on 2026-06-16, the latest Tdap dispensing day, medical home -> 0.00; baseline -> 32.00.
  - medication_check_visit_copay (parameter, cross-difficulty rx): sick visit C26-0602-44190 on 2026-06-02, the latest maintenance refill day, medical home -> 1.00; baseline -> 33.00.
  - coordinated_followup_copay (parameter, care): in-person follow-up 2026-07-06 AND reached transition call 2026-07-02 -> 0.00; baseline -> 32.00.
  Reversal = 10.00 + 2 x 4.00 + 5.00 + 5.00 + 4.00 + 5.00 = 37.00.

5. Base-invariant card. plan_claim_adjusted (both re-ratings) inherits plan_evt_claim_adjustment: original_is_paid (C26-0714-45006 and C26-0706-45077 adjudication_status paid), adjust_window (anchor booked_date 2026-07-22 / 2026-07-14; count from the day after, 365 days inclusive; review 2026-07-28 is day 6 / day 14; day 366 would fail), adjust_once (no plan_claim_adjusted row references either claim). Declared overwrites: the one-claim whole-reversal sentence and the reason list (re-ratings reverse part of copays, reason none). plan_cost_share_refund inherits plan_evt_cost_share_cap refund_once_per_claim (no refund row references C26-0714-45006 in period 2026); overwrites declared for the calendar-period measure, the period-income sentence and the crossing-claim booking sentence. plan_premium_paid: plan_evt_premium has no gate on payments (policy_scope); the oldest-first allocation sentence is overwritten by 'settles that month alone'.

6. Business-object card. Refund: membership <m0>, booked against the most recently booked copay claim C26-0714-45006 (booked 2026-07-22), period 2026; excluded: ended-spell claims C25-0909-38614 and C25-1014-39322 (membership <m0p>, copay 0.00). Own-PCP batch: specialist-rated claims of NPI 1588392047 (superseded, 2025-11-01..2026-02-28) and 1467283015 from 2026-03; excluded C26-0112-41640 and pulmonologist NPI 1356620841 claims. Office batch: logged well/telehealth-well/same-day/vaccine-day/follow-up office visits; the entry names C26-0706-45077. Payment: coverage month 2026-08 (bill 35.00 posted 2026-07-01, due 2026-07-20); 2026-07 is paid (PRP-5736420).

7. Seed rows. Claims (24 on the open spell) carry the category schedule copays; premiums: 10 bills (9 at 20.00, 2026-08 at 35.00 billed during a temporary higher income on the state file, contrary to continuous eligibility) and 9 payments; pcp: two assignments + 12 visit log rows; rx: coverage + 7 fills; auth: 2 authorizations; care: episode + 4 activities; ride: benefit + 7 completed trips. Deleting the DME authorization drops the cap to 4% (refund changes); deleting the ride trips drops travel relief; deleting the care episode changes admission relief, care reward, stacking and schedule. No row ignites an obligation outside this tree: no therapy authorization received in the window, no ambulance claim, no refund or adjustment already booked (both task-1 re-ratings evaluate to 0.00 here).

8. Persona. Hurried mother on a work break; volunteers only the goal (check copays against the yearly limit, refund the excess) and true context (asthma, three hospital stays, copays at most visits). Gives Medicaid ID, DOB, phone, ZIP, SSN last four only when asked. Passive: general go-ahead to correct the account; pays herself by phone with her debit card only after the representative says something must be settled and hands it over; does not know or guess the amount; closes when told the refund is booked.

9. Standard solution. find_customers(PR17305926) -> verify (PR17305926, 2016-11-03) -> memberships -> claims (by customer; exclude ended spell) -> premiums -> pcp assignments -> pcp visits -> rx coverage -> rx fills -> auth -> care enrollments -> care activities -> ride benefits -> ride trips -> own-PCP re-rating 36.00 on C26-0714-45006 -> office re-rating 37.00 on C26-0706-45077 -> hand over payment: membership <m0>, 2026-08, 13.75, phone_ivr -> refund 267.97 on C26-0714-45006, period 2026.

10. Verification. Scratch scripts (sim.py/harness.py) replay the gold writes with the real tools and evaluate every compute through check_compute.build_env/eval_compute at each write's handling time; outputs: K1 36.0, W 37.0, P2 13.75, P1 267.97; skip sensitivity P1 = 303.97 / 304.97 / 219.22. Gates run: check_extended, check_task_tools, replay_tasks, check_solvability, check_compute, check_grounding, check_cross_fire with --task 0 -> all OK. check_traceability not run (KB not yet published).

11. Draft recomputation from the visible context: from the published rules (baseline + factor ladders), the tool schemas, the persona and the share-tool returns, a reader derives the same four writes in the same dependency order; the only reachable choice points (which claim each entry names, which coverage month, payment method) are pinned by explicit sentences quoted in argument_uniqueness_tracing.

Revision log: (a) K1 scope baseline equalled result (Jan-12 visit swapped with Jan-20) -> added the 2025-12-16 previous-provider visit; (b) P2 care reward was decorative under max-stacking -> stacking tier changed to averaging; (c) replay closure flagged 5 unread rows -> claims read by customer, rx coverage read added, unused card notices dropped; (d) payment tool now settles the month (billed amount leaves the balance) so the zero-balance state is reachable.

Round 2 (audit audits/policy_task/member_cost_sharing_and_renewal): F1 — the own-PCP and office re-ratings declare an overwrite of plan_evt_copay's schedule sentence; the office re-rating no longer leaves any copay on preventive care (all logged well-child visits return in full; the old telehealth well-child tier, immunization-visit tier and well-child schedule were replaced by telehealth sick-visit, vaccine-day sick-visit and medication-check factors; world: the 2026-03-24 telehealth visit is a sick visit, added telehealth sick visit C26-0210-41955 on the superseded log and medication-check visit C26-0602-44190). F2 — every rule says rounded half up and every RND carries the half-up guard; the cap tie now resolves to 602.78 on both faces. F3 — window sentences restated in rolling whole-month terms. F5 — the continuous-eligibility months run are counted from the later of coverage start and the current eligibility period start. F7 — telehealth follow-up and initial-appointment counts read only the current assignment's log. F9 — the carry-over sentence of plan_evt_cost_share_cap is declared superseded. F10 — the health-home visit copay is 0.50, distinct from every initial-appointment tier.
user_scenario:
You are Ingrid Halvorsen-Mbeki, and you are calling Prairie Ridge Health Plan member services on a Tuesday morning from the break room at work about your nine-year-old daughter, Zuri Halvorsen-Mbeki, who is on Prairie Ridge CHIP Kids. You are her mother and you handle everything about her coverage. Zuri has asthma and this has been a hard year: three hospital stays since last winter, a lung specialist, clinic visits, lab work, and you have paid a copay at almost every one of them. A friend at church told you that CHIP families have a yearly limit on what they pay out of pocket, tied to income, and you are sure you are past it. What you want is simple: have Prairie Ridge check what you have paid against that limit, and if you paid more than you should have, give the extra back for Zuri. You don't know how the limit is figured and you don't have a total in your head; you'd like it settled on this call if it can be.

You speak plainly and a little hurriedly, because your break is short. When the representative asks for details to find and verify Zuri, you answer only what is asked, one or two items at a time: her Medicaid ID is PR17305926, her date of birth is 2016-11-03 (November 3, 2016), the phone number on her file is 4025510462, and your home ZIP code is 68108. If asked for the last four of her Social Security number you give 1583.

You are happy for the representative to look through Zuri's records and to fix whatever needs fixing on her account before working out the refund; you give that go-ahead as soon as they ask. If the representative tells you that something on Zuri's account has to be settled or paid by you before the refund can be worked out, you say you will pay it yourself right now, and when they hand the payment over to you, you pay by phone with your debit card for the amount and month they give you. You have no amount or confirmation number in mind ahead of time; you repeat the confirmation number only if the payment gives you one and they ask for it.

If the representative asks how much you think you are owed, you say you honestly don't know and want it checked against the records, not guessed. If they read you a figure you simply ask whether that is final. Once they tell you the refund for Zuri has been booked, you thank them, say that's all you needed today, and end the call.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.related_claim_number: Value C26-0714-45006. Basis: the rule of the own-PCP visit re-rating says 'The re-rating is booked as one adjustment entry that names the most recently serviced claim of the batch as its original claim'; the batch (claims C26-1216-41002 and C26-0120-41793 by the superseded provider NPI 1588392047, C26-0310-42741 and C26-0714-45006 by the current provider NPI 1467283015 on or after 2026-03-01) has 2026-07-14 as its latest service date. Uniqueness: C26-0112-41640 (NPI 1467283015 on 2026-01-12, before the assignment took effect) is outside the batch, and no other batch claim is serviced later than 2026-07-14.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.reversal_amount: Value 36.00. Batch copays 40.00 over 4 visits (scope tier: previous assignment superseded and current member-selected, so current-provider visits from 2026-03 plus previous-provider visits); re-rated total 4.00 = (4 - 1 telehealth - 1 initial appointment) x 2.00 medical-home copay + 1 x 0.00 + 1 x 0.00 (initial appointment 9 days after the 2026-03-01 effective date); reversal = 40.00 - 4.00 = 36.00.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.related_claim_number: Value C26-0706-45077. Basis: 'The office-visit re-rating is booked as one adjustment entry that names the most recently serviced office-visit claim of the member's primary care providers as its original claim'. The office-visit (primary care visit category) claims billed by NPI 1467283015 or 1588392047 are dated 2026-02-17, 03-24, 04-21 (two), 06-16 and 07-06; 2026-07-06 is the latest. Uniqueness: the later claims C26-0707-45109 (behavioral health) and C26-0709-45140 (lab) are not office visits of the primary care providers.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.reversal_amount: Value 37.00. Well-child visits on any primary care log in the window 2 x 5.00 returned in full (preventive care carries no copay); telehealth sick visits 2 (current and superseded logs, a superseded assignment exists) x (5.00 - 1.00); same-day sick 1 x (5.00 - 0.00); vaccine-day sick 1 x (5.00 - 0.00); medication check on the latest refill day 1 x (5.00 - 1.00); coordinated follow-up 1 x (5.00 - 0.00) with a reached transition call on 2026-07-02; total 37.00 (half-up rounding).

evaluation_criteria.necessity: plan_ext_past_due_premium_payment computes payment_amount; the over-cap refund on an open membership is fixed only after the premium balance stands at zero.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.membership_id: Value 55b307b5-de4a-4b28-9c1d-2933d60e4f0a: the open CHIP Kids membership returned by find_plan_memberships, read out to the mother with the hand-over; the only membership carrying a premium bill.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.coverage_month: Value 2026-08. Basis: 'The family's phone payment is made for the most recently billed coverage month once that month's due date has passed'; the latest bill in the premium ledger is coverage month 2026-08 posted 2026-07-01, due 2026-07-20, and the review date 2026-07-28 is past it. Uniqueness: 2026-07 already carries payment PRP-5736420; no later month is billed.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.payment_amount: Value 13.75. Month rate 20.00: the 2026-08 bill is 35.00, above the most recent paid amount 20.00, while continuous eligibility from 2025-11-01 has run 8 of 12 months; rewards: well-child 3.00 (2 well-child visits logged, medical-home practice), refill 2.00 (4 fills in 6 months, no rejection), care 2.50 (active episode, 2 reached contacts in 3 months), steady payer 1.50 (7 portal vs 2 phone payments); stacking (medical home and active episode) = (3.00+2.50)/2 + 2.00 + 1.50 = 6.25; payment = 20.00 - 6.25 = 13.75.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.payment_method: Value phone_ivr. Basis: the tool docstring: 'phone_ivr when paying by card or bank draft over the phone payment line'; the mother says she will 'pay by phone with your debit card'. Uniqueness: online_portal, mail_check and money_order are other channels she does not use, and not_applicable never applies to a family payment.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.related_claim_number: Value C26-0714-45006. Basis: 'The refund is booked as one refund entry against the most recently booked medical claim that carries a copay in the counting window'; its booked date 2026-07-22 is the latest booked date among copay-carrying claims (next latest C26-0709-45140 booked 2026-07-16). Uniqueness: the adjustment entries booked today are not medical claims carrying a copay.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.cost_share_period: Value 2026: 'carrying that claim's cost-sharing period'; claim C26-0714-45006 carries cost-sharing period 2026 (annual CHIP cap label).
argument_uniqueness_tracing.refund_amount: Value 267.97. Counted total 610.75 = medical copays net 417.00 (after the two re-rating entries) + refunds booked 0.00 + pharmacy 0.00 + counted premium 193.75 (balance now zero, so premiums paid in the window including today's 13.75); cap = RND half up(2679.00 x 9 months x 2.5% / 100) - admission 150.00 - medication 60.00 - travel 50.00 = 342.78; refund = 610.75 - 342.78 = 267.97.

edges.policy_source: On a membership that is still open, the over-cap refund is fixed only after the premium balance on the membership stands at zero.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The three prerequisites are parallel and commute: the own-PCP re-rating reads only booked specialist claims (event plan_claim_booked) and PCP records, the office-visit re-rating reads only PCP logs, pharmacy and care records, and the payment reads only the premium ledger, PCP, pharmacy and care records; none reads what another writes (adjustment rows are not booked claims, a premium row is not a claim). Replaying them in the orders K1-W-P2 and P2-W-K1 gives the same terminal ledger and the same values 36.00 / 37.00 / 13.75 / 267.97 (sim.py run).

Without the re-rating entry the medical copays stay 36.00 higher and the refund becomes 303.97 instead of 267.97.
